metadata.title: Replication package: Level Breaks and Finite-Sample GLS Detrending: The Point-Optimal Unit Root Test and the Purchasing Power Parity Puzzle
metadata.description: Replication code and public data for the paper 'Level Breaks and Finite-Sample GLS Detrending: The Point-Optimal Unit Root Test and the Purchasing Power Parity Puzzle'. A single Numba-compiled numerical kernel (src/mlb/kernel_numba.py) drives all Monte Carlo; the package is numba-only by design (no NumPy fallback ships). A single entry point, replicate.py, reproduces every printed exhibit: it reads the frozen golden outputs by default (--quick) and regenerates from scratch on demand (--full). Five self-contained doors under section_replications/ organize the work: (1) critical_values -- the finite-sample point-optimal calibration, tabulating the P_T statistic and the four M-class statistics (MZ_alpha, MZ_t, MSB, MPT) at the 1/2.5/5/10 percent points by (m, T) at cbar=-7, produced by a K=20 block design of 165,000 replications per block (3,300,000 per cell); (2) robustness -- the AR(1) size/power study; (3) bootstrap_empirical -- the PPP application (sieve and wild bootstrap, median-unbiased half-lives) and the Pesaran cross-sectional-dependence diagnostic (pesaran_cd.py); (4) supplement -- the online-supplement S2 and section 6.3 numerics (empirical modulus, dependence PMF and bound, assumption checks); (5) figures -- figure rendering from the doors' output. All printed tables and figures reproduce from files inside the package.

metadata.title: Replication Package: The Illusion of Cognitive Sovereignty / Die Illusion kognitiver Souveränität?
metadata.description:
Abstract of the corresponding thesis

Artificial intelligence increasingly assumes advisory and executive roles in organisational decision-making. The European AI Act prohibits systems that materially distort decision-making through covert or manipulative techniques, yet leaves open at what intensity such distortion occurs. This thesis determines that tipping point experimentally. In a 3x4 mixed design, 136 participants faced four escalating levels of persuasion in realistic B2B procurement scenarios, ranging from a neutral baseline through a covert structural nudge and emotional framing to overt algorithmic flattery (sycophancy). One group received the treatments framed as AI interaction, the other did not. In parallel, four large language models completed the identical design as demographically conditioned twins of the human participants (silicon sampling). Decision resilience was captured by the newly developed Cognitive Resilience Index, and the discrepancy between recognised influence and actual behaviour by the Sovereignty Gap. Resilience does not collapse under the overtly manipulative levels but under the covert nudge, where the share of risky decisions rises from 26 to 69 percent. This tipping point occurs at the same position in all four language models. The AI-framed group recognised the influence significantly better yet demonstrably did not behave more resiliently.

metadata.title: Replication Package for "Quantum-Enhanced Financial Volatility Forecasting and Portfolio Risk Management: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Framework"
metadata.description:
This replication package accompanies the revised manuscript “Quantum-Enhanced Financial Volatility Forecasting and Portfolio Risk Management: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Framework,” submitted to Computational Economics under manuscript ID CSEM-D-25-00573.

The package provides replication and transparency materials for the revised study. It includes synthetic train/validation/test data, figure source data, manuscript table source data, table and figure regeneration scripts, validation scripts, a reproducibility matrix, a reproducibility-scope statement, configuration logs, and supplementary documentation.

The package is designed to support transparent review under data-sharing constraints. The manuscript uses public market data and licensed/proprietary financial data. Licensed Bloomberg-derived data and any proprietary financial database are not redistributed in this package. Instead, the package provides a synthetic dataset with the same feature schema and documented workflow, enabling replication of the preprocessing structure, table-generation logic, figure-generation logic, and manuscript-aligned result traceability.

The materials are intended to make the revised manuscript auditable with respect to task separation, model-result reporting, noise-mitigation overhead, and NISQ-scale resource accounting. The package does not claim to reproduce live IBM Quantum backend queue latency, because queue latency depends on backend availability, calibration windows, and platform-specific scheduling conditions.

Package contents include:
- synthetic raw and processed financial-feature datasets;
- train, validation, and test splits;
- figure source data for QAOA scaling, portfolio Sharpe ratio, volatility forecasting accuracy, accuracy-runtime trade-off, and noise-mitigation overhead;
- manuscript table source data in CSV and LaTeX formats;
- scripts for synthetic data generation, manuscript table regeneration, figure regeneration, and package validation;
- reproducibility matrix linking manuscript claims to data files and scripts;
- reproducibility scope statement clarifying what is fully reproducible, partially reproducible, and not redistributable;
- configuration logs for QAOA, QNN, and QSVM experiments;
- SHA256 manifest for file-integrity verification.

This package should be interpreted as a synthetic-data replication and source-ledger package for review and transparency, not as a redistribution of proprietary financial data.

metadata.title: Replication package: AI, Verification, and the Reversal of the Division of Labor
metadata.description:
Replication package for:

Hsu, S.-H. (2026). "AI, Verification, and the Reversal of the Division of Labor." Economics Letters.

The paper is a theoretical note and contains no empirical data. This package contains the code that (1) generates Figure 1 directly from the paper's closed-form expressions, and (2) independently verifies every analytical claim in the paper against numerical solutions.

Contents:
- code/generate_Figure_1.py -- produces Figure 1 (both panels)
- code/verify_propositions.py -- 39 numerical checks of the paper's propositions, closed-form expressions, and reported constants
- output/ -- the resulting figure files and verification log

Verification: each of the 39 checks compares an analytical claim against an independent numerical method (global minimization, root finding, finite differences, or quadrature) rather than a rearrangement of the same algebra. All 39 checks pass (see output/verification_log.txt).

Both scripts are self-contained, deterministic, and depend only on NumPy, SciPy, and Matplotlib (see requirements.txt). Full instructions are in README.md.

Both scripts were written with the assistance of Claude (Anthropic, 2026), as disclosed in the paper; their outputs were independently verified and the same standards of validity and reproducibility apply as to code written without such assistance.

Code is released under the MIT License.

metadata.title: Economic NMPC toolkit for variable-speed wind turbines: Supplementary code and data
metadata.description:
This repository contains the MATLAB implementation of an economic nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) framework for variable-speed wind turbines, developed as supplementary material for the paper "Economic nonlinear MPC for wind turbines: A systematic framework for constraint enforcement" (García-Violini et al., 2026).

The repository is organised as a reusable toolkit (core/) and a complete paper replication package (paper_replication/), and includes pre-computed simulation data for immediate result verification.

Key features:

  • Standalone economic NMPC solver with eight operational constraints spanning electrical, mechanical, and actuation domains
  • Drivetrain net-torque bound with rainflow-based damage equivalent load (DEL) fatigue assessment
  • Causal autoregressive wind speed predictor (AR, order 50)
  • Generic pipeline applicable to any variable-speed turbine via a commented parameter template
  • Five worked examples: quickstart, custom-turbine adaptation, constraint tuning, case comparison, AR predictor demonstration
  • Pre-computed results for all five simulation cases (FF, NMPC-A, NMPC-B, NMPC-C, NMPC-B')
  • Complete documentation: getting-started guide, per-constraint calibration guide, parameter adaptation guide, FAQ

Requirements: MATLAB R2024b or later, Optimization Toolbox (fmincon). Signal Processing Toolbox (rainflow) required only for the DEL fatigue case; a fallback is provided automatically if unavailable.

metadata.title: Replication package: mutation testing for competency question coverage evaluators
metadata.description:
Code and derived data for the article Mutation testing for competency question coverage evaluators.

Ontology engineering pipelines built on large language models close a generate-evaluate loop in which the model judges whether the ontology it produced answers its competency questions, and that verdict decides when the loop stops. The usual way to check such an evaluator is agreement with a reference standard, and none is available for the generated-ontology setting: executing a published formalisation against a generated ontology first requires deciding which generated term stands for which term in the query, and that decision carries the verdict.

This package validates coverage evaluators by manipulation instead. A battery of 14 mutation operators changes each ontology in ways whose effect on coverage is settled in advance. CQ-destroying operators remove the axioms a question is answered through, each following a documented modelling pitfall, with the loss of coverage confirmed per mutant by execution. CQ-preserving operators change the ontology while provably preserving every entailment over the question's signature, verified mechanically. Every evaluator - the executable criterion, three open-weights judges, and two surface baselines - is scored on how many injected faults it detects and how many preserving mutants leave its verdict undisturbed. Neither rate needs a reference verdict, a human label, or a vocabulary alignment, because every comparison is between two versions of one ontology.

The package contains the generation, execution, judging and mutation harnesses, the analysis scripts, and the derived artifacts: the generated ontologies, 938 operator applications yielding 761 mutants over 117 competency questions in 27 requirement sets, the execution verdicts, the judge verdicts, and the analysis outputs behind each table in the article. Every number in the article is written into the manuscript as a macro by the analysis code, and the resulting macro file ships with the package so that any figure can be traced back to the run that produced it.

The source corpora and the model weights are not redistributed. They are fetched at pinned revisions and verified against recorded tree hashes; see data/README.md for provenance and terms of use.

metadata.title: Replication Package for "Déjà vu? Redundant Dependencies in Terraform"
metadata.description:
To be able to use the replication package follow the steps:

  • Install Docker by following the instructions for your operating system described here.
  • Run docker load < depends-off-replication-package.tar in the folder with the tar file previously downloaded.
  • Run docker run -it --name depends-off depends-off-replication:v4 /bin/bash.
  • To be able to return to the container, run docker attach depends-off.

The docker container is ready to use!

It is important to mention that these instructions were tested with a MacOS Tahoe 26.2 system. For other operating systems, some adjustments may need to be made.

After these steps, check the README on the root folder.

Running on x86 machines

To run this image in an x86 machine, you might need to use emulation.

  • On the first time, run docker run --privileged --rm tonistiigi/binfmt --install all.
  • Then, simply add the flag --platform=linux/arm64 on the docker run command shown in the replication steps.

The Docker container includes depends-off's code, the code to replicate the evaluation, and the obtained results.
